events.content:
Done. PPR is enabled and working. In this Next.js 16 version, `experimental.ppr` is deprecated — PPR is now controlled by the top-level `cacheComponents` option, which I set in `next.config.ts:4`. The build confirms it: - `Cache Components enabled` - Route `/` shows `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content The existing `page.tsx` already wraps the async data-fetching components (`ProductList`, `Recommendations`) in ``, which is exactly what PPR needs: the static shell (`

Store

`) is pre-rendered at build time, while the dynamic parts inside each `Suspense` boundary stream in at request time.
